chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Short tributes: Wes Montgomery, Slide Hampton and Eric Dolphy
summary: Baker calls Wes the greatest jazz guitarist, Slide his alter ego and best trombonist in the business, and Dolphy an unrealized talent who died at 34.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Wes Montgomery: a big inspiration; [a] very, very close friend; [the] greatest guitarist of all time, in my estimation – jazz guitarist – [his] face could light – [his] smile could light up a room. I always think that when I remember him.

Slide Hampton: alter ego; [a] very, very close friend; and one of maybe my two or three favorite writers and composers. And I think, probably, now that J. J.’s not playing, probably the best jazz trombonist in the business.

Eric Dolphy: groundbreaker; [a] very, very good friend; unrealized gargantuan talent. [He] died far too young, age 34, before he had a chance to really leave the mark he would have left, had he lived another 30 years.
